title: SimPO: Simple Preference Optimization with a Reference-Free Reward
data_curation: Preference data is built on top of UltraFeedback prompts, used in two ways. In the Base setup, the SFT model is trained on UltraChat-200k, then preference optimization runs on the original UltraFeedback pairs (following Zephyr). In the Instruct setup, the authors regenerate an on-policy preference dataset: for each UltraFeedback prompt they sample 5 responses from the off-the-shelf instruct model at temperature 0.8, score them with PairRM (llm-blender/PairRM), and keep the highest-scoring as y_w and lowest as y_l; generation is a single pass, not iterative. For the strongest Gemma-2-9B-it and an updated Llama-3-Instruct-v0.2 run, they swap the scorer for the stronger ArmoRM (RLHFlow/ArmoRM-Llama3-8B-v0.1), which markedly lifts quality (e.g., +9.0 AlpacaEval 2 LC). No explicit de-duplication or filtering beyond reward-model ranking is described.
curriculum: A standard two-stage offline pipeline: SFT then single-stage preference optimization (no iterative/online loops). Base setup: pretrain base model -> SFT on UltraChat-200k (lr 2e-5, batch 128, seq len 2048, 1 epoch, cosine schedule with 10% warmup) -> preference optimization on UltraFeedback. Instruct setup: skip SFT, start from an off-the-shelf instruct checkpoint -> preference optimization on the on-policy regenerated pairs. ORPO is the only baseline that can drop the SFT stage, but for fairness it is also started from the same SFT checkpoint. Preference optimization uses batch 128, 1 epoch, method-specific learning rates (SimPO lr 3e-7 to 1e-6), Adam. The paper explicitly restricts itself to offline, non-iterative training.
method: SimPO is a reference-free offline preference optimization algorithm with two key designs. (1) A length-normalized implicit reward equal to the average log probability of a response: r(x,y) = (beta/|y|) * sum log pi_theta(y_i | x, y<i), which matches the likelihood metric used at inference (beam search / multiple-choice scoring) and removes DPO's train/inference mismatch; summed log-prob is avoided because it biases toward longer sequences. (2) A target reward margin gamma > 0 inserted into the Bradley-Terry objective so the winning reward must exceed the losing one by at least gamma. The loss is L = -E log sigma( (beta/|y_w|) log pi(y_w|x) - (beta/|y_l|) log pi(y_l|x) - gamma ). No reference model is needed, cutting runtime ~20% and GPU memory ~10% vs DPO, and no explicit KL regularization is used (low KL is maintained empirically via small lr, diverse data, and LLM robustness). Good defaults: beta in [2.0,2.5], gamma in [0.5,1.5].
eval_metrics: Three open-ended chat benchmarks: AlpacaEval 2 (805 prompts; length-controlled LC and raw WR win rate vs GPT-4 Turbo, pairwise judge), Arena-Hard v0.1 (500 queries; WR vs GPT-4-0314), and MT-Bench (80 questions; 1-10 single-answer grading by GPT-4/GPT-4 Turbo). Downstream tasks via HuggingFace Open Leaderboard: MMLU, ARC, HellaSwag, TruthfulQA, Winograd, GSM8K. Real-user evaluation on Chatbot Arena (LMSYS). Authors note MT-Bench has poor separability and Arena-Hard is the hardest. Headline: SimPO beats DPO by up to +6.4 AlpacaEval 2 LC and +7.5 Arena-Hard WR; it beats the best baseline by 3.6-4.8 AlpacaEval 2 LC across settings.
key_results: Gemma-2-9B-it-SimPO reaches 72.4% LC win rate on AlpacaEval 2, 59.1% WR on Arena-Hard, and ranks 1st among <10B models on Chatbot Arena (lifting Gemma-2-9B-it from 36th to 25th overall). SimPO outperforms DPO by up to 6.4 pts (AlpacaEval 2 LC) and 7.5 pts (Arena-Hard), while cutting DPO runtime ~20% and GPU memory ~10%.
evolution_note: SimPO builds directly on DPO (2023) and contemporaneous reference-free work such as ORPO, reacting to DPO's mismatch between its log-ratio reward and the average-log-likelihood used at generation, plus the cost of carrying a reference model. In the 2024 alignment landscape it became a widely adopted lightweight DPO replacement and motivated follow-up on length-controlled, reference-free objectives and on adding SFT-regularization to preserve reasoning/math ability.
